question: Fill in the blanks: A new All-India Service can be created by a resolution passed in the _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **new All-India Service** can be created under **Article 312** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• **Article 312** provides that the **Rajya Sabha**, by passing a resolution with a **two-thirds majority** of its members present and voting, can authorize the Parliament to create a new All-India Service.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** does not have the power to initiate or pass a resolution for creating an All-India Service. *Hence, option 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **State Legislatures** do not hold any authority to create a new All-India Service under the Constitution. Their role in such matters is limited to other state-specific powers. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• The **NITI Aayog Council** does not have constitutional powers to create an All-India Service. It primarily serves as a policy think tank and advisory body. *Hence, option 4 is incorrect.*
 
• Once the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution, the **Parliament** enacts a law to establish the new All-India Service. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 312 of the Constitution:**

 
 
• **Article 312** empowers the Rajya Sabha to recommend the creation of new All-India Services like the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** and **Indian Police Service (IPS)**.
 
• This provision ensures uniformity in administration and governance across the country, enhancing coordination between the Centre and the states.
 
 
 
• **All-India Services:**
 
 
• Currently, the **All-India Services** include the **Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Police Service (IPS),** and the **Indian Forest Service (IFS).**
 
• These services are governed by central rules but cater to both the Centre and the states, ensuring administrative uniformity.
 
• **Example:** Officers in the **IAS** are responsible for implementing policies at both central and state levels.
 
 
 
• **Procedure for Creating All-India Services:**
 
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution authorizing the Parliament to legislate on the matter.
 
• The Parliament then enacts a law to establish the new service.
 
• This procedure ensures that states are consulted indirectly since representatives in the Rajya Sabha represent their respective states.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of All-India Services:**

 
 
• These services are unique as their members are recruited by the Centre but serve both the Centre and the states.
 
• They play a crucial role in maintaining administrative continuity and enhancing governance efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• **1947:** The Indian Administrative Service was established as the successor to the Imperial Civil Service.
 
• **1951:** The Indian Police Service and Indian Forest Service were created as All-India Services to maintain law and order and manage forest resources effectively.
